lesson_title: Scales and Street Maps: Reading Distance, Direction and Cost
hook_text: Photocopy a map and the scale printed on it becomes a lie. One thing on the page keeps telling the truth.
clip_script: The map says 1 to 50 000. Your route measures 7 centimetres. Multiply: 350 000 centimetres. Tidy up: 3 500 metres — 3,5 kilometres. That's the whole method: measure, multiply, tidy. Now shrink that map on a photocopier to fit your pocket. Every road just got smaller — but the printed ratio still says 1 to 50 000. It's lying now. Down in the corner, though, sits a little striped bar — and the bar shrank WITH the roads. Stripe for stripe, it still tells the truth on any copy, at any size. That's why real maps carry both. Now make the map pay for the trip. Road map, 1 to 150 000, route is 12 centimetres — 18 kilometres. At 60 an hour: 18 divided by 60 is 0,3 hours. Not 30 minutes — 0,3 times 60 is 18 minutes. The car drinks 8 litres per 100 k's, so 1,44 litres, R33,84 each way. Taxi wants R52 return. Alone? Take the taxi. Four of you? The car's R67,68 beats the taxi's R208 by more than R140. The map just saved you money.
visual_style: A street map of Polokwane under a moving ruler; the map sliding through a photocopier and shrinking while the printed ratio flashes red and the bar scale glows green; the route unrolling into kilometres, minutes and a petrol pump display.
mood: Practical and road-trip ready, the confidence of a navigator who has never been lost.
pacing: Measured through the three-step method, a sharp gotcha at the photocopier, brisk acceleration through the time-fuel-money chain.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and turn any map into distances, minutes and rands.
